questions.text: Do you enforce unique user accounts with strong passwords for all staff accessing company systems?
Do you require multi-factor authentication (MFA) for critical systems and remote access?
Do you review and revoke access promptly when employees change roles or leave?
Do you apply least-privilege, granting staff only the access they need for their role?
Do you take regular backups of critical data and systems?
Do you periodically test restoring from backups to confirm they work?
Do you keep at least one backup copy offline or in a separate location from production?
Do you apply security updates to operating systems and software in a timely manner?
Do you maintain an inventory of software and systems that need patching?
Do you track and remediate known vulnerabilities on internet-facing systems?
Do you have a documented plan describing how to respond to a security incident?
Do staff know how to report a suspected security incident, and to whom?
Do you keep logs that would help you investigate a security incident?
Do you assess the security practices of third-party vendors before granting them access or data?
Do your contracts with vendors include security and data-protection obligations?
Do you maintain an up-to-date list of vendors that handle your data or systems?
Do you encrypt sensitive data at rest (e.g. databases, backups, laptops)?
Do you encrypt sensitive data in transit (e.g. HTTPS/TLS for all services)?
Do you classify data so staff know what is sensitive and how to handle it?
Do you restrict and monitor who can access customer and financial data?
